request.system: You assist requirements analysts who apply the OGORE framework. You refine one IT goal of an organization's Initial Goal Tree Model by adapting validated goal patterns retrieved from a Goal Knowledge Base. Use only the six OGORE element types: Goal, Task, Resource, Actor, Belief, Constraint. Do not invent KPI values.

messages.content:
RETRIEVED PATTERNS:
[SKB-05/G3] (similarity 0.5823)
PATTERN SKB-05 | insurance company (synthetic) | customer service; governance of an LLM-based assistant with retrieval
Organization goal: offer fast, correct, and accountable answers to customers
IT goal G3: AI risks governed (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G3-K1 Model or prompt changes recorded and approved before release (target 100%); G3-K2 Risk assessment of the assistant reviewed (target every 6 months)
  Tasks: Keep a model and prompt change register; Review the AI risk assessment with the risk committee
  Resources: Change register; AI risk register
  Actors: AI Product Owner; Risk Officer
  Beliefs: none
  Constraints: Customer personal data is not sent to the model provider beyond the session
  Rational statement: A change register makes every model or prompt change attributable, which the evaluation KPI depends on.

[SKB-05/G2] (similarity 0.5265)
PATTERN SKB-05 | insurance company (synthetic) | customer service; governance of an LLM-based assistant with retrieval
Organization goal: offer fast, correct, and accountable answers to customers
IT goal G2: Assistant answers grounded and traceable (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Answers citing an approved source document (target 100%); G2-K2 Answers on topics outside the approved corpus that are escalated to a human agent (target 100%)
  Tasks: Retrieve answers only from the approved policy corpus; Escalate out-of-scope questions to a human agent; Run a monthly evaluation on a fixed test set
  Resources: Approved policy corpus; Evaluation test set
  Actors: AI Product Owner; Customer Service Agent
  Beliefs: Customers act on the assistant's answers
  Constraints: The assistant does not give answers that commit the company financially
  Conflict resolved: broader corpus would answer more questions but include unapproved drafts -> only approved documents enter the corpus; coverage gaps are filled by escalation

[SKB-01/G2] (similarity 0.4841)
PATTERN SKB-01 | medium-sized food and beverage distributor (synthetic) | wholesale distribution; order-to-cash and lot traceability
Organization goal: deliver complete and traceable orders to retail customers
IT goal G2: Customer orders recorded accurately (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Order lines matching the customer purchase order (target 99.5%); G2-K2 Order confirmation sent after entry (target within 30 minutes)
  Tasks: Capture customer purchase order with price list validation; Confirm order to customer
  Resources: Customer price list; Order management module
  Actors: Sales Administrator; Customer
  Beliefs: Price lists are customer specific
  Constraints: A confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request
  Conflict resolved: lot scanning slows picking and delays confirmation -> confirm the order at entry and scan lots at picking, so confirmation time is unaffected

[SKB-08/G1] (similarity 0.4314)
PATTERN SKB-08 | manufacturing company (synthetic) | procurement; supplier invoice matching
Organization goal: pay suppliers correctly and on time
IT goal G1: Supplier invoices matched before payment
  KPIs: G1-K1 Invoices three-way matched (target 100%); G1-K2 Invoices paid on due date (target 98%)
  Tasks: Match invoice, purchase order, and goods receipt; Hold mismatched invoices for review
  Resources: Accounts payable module
  Actors: Accounts Payable Clerk; Purchasing Officer
  Beliefs: none
  Constraints: Payment runs need a second approver

QUERY:
GOAL: G07 "Ordering assistant governed as an AI system"; parent G01 "Regulated order-to-delivery controlled and secure"
DOMAIN: pharmaceutical distribution to hospitals; organization type: medium-sized distributor with an order portal and an LLM-based ordering assistant
KPIS: G07-K1 = Assistant answers that cite an approved source (100%); G07-K2 = Hospital-specific prices disclosed to another hospital in the monthly audit (0); G07-K3 = Answers rated correct in the monthly evaluation (>= 95%); G07-K4 = Model and prompt changes approved before release (100%)
ACTORS IN SCOPE: Hospital Buyer; Sales Administrator; Responsible Pharmacist; Quality Assurance Officer; IT Security Officer; Data Protection Officer; AI Product Owner
BELIEFS: The assistant runs on an external model provider
CONSTRAINTS: The assistant cannot place or change an order without the buyer's confirmation; Patient identifiers are not sent to the language model provider

TASK: (1) Rank the retrieved patterns by relevance to the query and state why each is relevant, citing its pattern ID. (2) Adapt them to the query and propose Tasks, Actors, Resources, Beliefs, and Constraints for the goal (and sub-goals only if the goal needs further decomposition). (3) Link every proposed element to the goal ID or to one of its KPI IDs, exactly as given in the query. (4) Draft one rational statement that explains how the goal and its elements serve the parent goal and its KPIs. (5) Give, for each element, the pattern ID it was adapted from; if it was not taken from a retrieved pattern, write UNGROUNDED. Every proposed element must respect the beliefs and constraints listed in the query.

ranked_patterns.relevance: Most relevant: it is the AI-governance sibling goal of an LLM assistant with retrieval and directly supplies the change-register and risk-review mechanics that G07-K4 (model and prompt changes approved before release, 100%) requires, plus the constraint pattern of not exposing protected personal data to the external model provider, which maps onto the query belief about the external provider and the patient-identifier constraint.

Second: it covers grounded and traceable assistant answers with an approved corpus, escalation of out-of-scope questions and a monthly evaluation on a fixed test set, which map almost one-to-one onto G07-K1 (answers citing an approved source, 100%) and G07-K3 (answers rated correct in the monthly evaluation, >= 95%), and its constraint on not committing the company financially is the ancestor of the query constraint that the assistant cannot place or change an order without buyer confirmation.

Third: it is a distribution order-capture pattern whose belief that price lists are customer specific and whose customer price list resource transfer to the hospital-specific contract prices behind G07-K2 (zero hospital-specific prices disclosed to another hospital in the monthly audit); it also contributes the Sales Administrator / customer actor pair present in the query scope.

Fourth and weakest: no AI content, but its control logic (hold mismatched items for review, payment runs need a second approver) is reusable as the approval gate and second-approver rule for releasing model or prompt changes under G07-K4, and as the hold-for-review handling of assistant outputs that fail the grounding check.

elements.text: Assistant answers grounded in the approved pharmaceutical corpus and traceable to a cited source
elements.justification: G07 carries four heterogeneous KPIs (grounding, confidentiality, answer quality, change control), so decomposition is needed; this sub-goal isolates the grounding and traceability concern carried by G07-K1, mirroring the pattern's 'Assistant answers grounded and traceable' goal.

elements.text: Hospital-specific commercial and patient data kept confidential in assistant interactions
elements.justification: Separates the confidentiality concern measured by G07-K2 and required by the patient-identifier constraint, adapting the pattern's customer-specific price list logic to a multi-hospital assistant.

elements.text: Model and prompt changes and AI risks governed under approval and review
elements.justification: Isolates the lifecycle-governance concern measured by G07-K4 and the periodic risk review, directly reusing the pattern's AI risk governance goal.

elements.text: Retrieve assistant answers only from the approved product, contract and regulatory corpus and attach the source citation to every answer
elements.justification: The pattern task 'Retrieve answers only from the approved policy corpus' is adapted to a pharmaceutical distributor; citing the retrieved document is what makes the 100% citation KPI measurable.

elements.text: Escalate out-of-scope, clinical or product-quality questions to the Responsible Pharmacist or Sales Administrator instead of answering
elements.justification: Adapts 'Escalate out-of-scope questions to a human agent'; coverage gaps left by the approved-only corpus are filled by humans so the citation KPI is not met by fabricating sources.

elements.text: Run a monthly evaluation of the assistant on a fixed test set of hospital ordering questions and record the correctness rating of each answer
elements.justification: Direct reuse of 'Run a monthly evaluation on a fixed test set'; it produces the measurement for the >= 95% correctness KPI.

elements.text: Hold or block assistant answers that fail the source-citation check and route them for human review before they reach the hospital buyer
elements.justification: Adapts 'Hold mismatched invoices for review' into a hold-for-review control on ungrounded answers, protecting the 100% citation target.

elements.text: Keep a register of every model version and prompt change with requester, approver and release date
elements.justification: Direct reuse of 'Keep a model and prompt change register'; attributability of each change is the evidence base for the 100% approval KPI.

elements.text: Approve each model or prompt change in the register before release and re-run the evaluation test set after release
elements.justification: Operationalises the pattern KPI 'changes recorded and approved before release' and links change control back to the G07-K3 quality evidence.

elements.text: Review the AI risk assessment of the ordering assistant with the Quality Assurance Officer, the IT Security Officer and the Data Protection Officer on a fixed periodic basis
elements.justification: Adapts 'Review the AI risk assessment with the risk committee' to the actors in scope; no KPI value is invented, the review cadence stays with the organization.

elements.text: Filter retrieval and answer generation by the buyer's hospital entitlement so that only that hospital's contract prices and order history can be used
elements.justification: Adapts 'Capture customer purchase order with price list validation' and the customer-specific price list belief into an entitlement filter, the preventive control behind the zero-disclosure KPI.

elements.text: Audit the monthly sample of assistant interaction logs for disclosure of another hospital's prices or contract terms
elements.justification: Adapts the register/review mechanic of the governance pattern into the detective audit explicitly named in the G07-K2 wording ('in the monthly audit').

elements.text: Remove patient identifiers and other patient-level data from prompts and retrieved snippets before any call to the external model provider
elements.justification: Adapts the pattern constraint on not sending customer personal data to the model provider into an executable task, required by the query constraint on patient identifiers and the belief about the external provider.

elements.text: Present the assistant's proposed order lines to the hospital buyer for explicit confirmation in the order portal before any order is created or changed
elements.justification: Adapts 'the assistant does not give answers that commit the company financially' and the pattern's confirm-to-customer logic to enforce the query constraint that the assistant cannot place or change an order alone.

elements.text: Approved corpus of product data sheets, framework contracts and regulatory/ordering procedures
elements.justification: Adaptation of the 'Approved policy corpus' resource; it is the only permitted retrieval source and therefore the basis of the citation KPI.

elements.text: Fixed evaluation test set of hospital ordering questions with expected answers
elements.justification: Direct reuse of the 'Evaluation test set' resource needed to compute the monthly correctness rating.

elements.text: Model and prompt change register
elements.justification: Direct reuse of the pattern resource 'Change register'; it stores the approval evidence counted by G07-K4.

elements.text: AI risk register for the ordering assistant
elements.justification: Direct reuse of the pattern resource 'AI risk register', supporting the periodic risk review of the assistant.

elements.text: Hospital-specific contract price list with entitlement rules
elements.justification: Adaptation of the 'Customer price list' resource; the entitlement rules make the per-hospital segregation enforceable and auditable.

elements.text: Assistant interaction log holding question, retrieved sources, cited answer and buyer identity
elements.justification: Adapted from the register-based accountability mechanic of the governance pattern; it is the evidence base for the monthly disclosure audit and for the citation and correctness checks.

elements.text: AI Product Owner
elements.justification: Direct reuse of the pattern actor; owns the change register and requests approval before each model or prompt release.

elements.text: Quality Assurance Officer
elements.justification: Adapts the pattern's Risk Officer role to the pharmaceutical quality function in scope; validates the monthly evaluation results and the risk review.

elements.text: IT Security Officer
elements.justification: Adapts the pattern's oversight actor to the security role in scope; owns the entitlement filtering and the monthly log audit for cross-hospital disclosure.

elements.text: Data Protection Officer
elements.justification: Adapts the pattern's governance oversight to the privacy role in scope, verifying that no patient identifiers leave for the external model provider.

elements.text: Responsible Pharmacist
elements.justification: Adapts the 'Customer Service Agent' escalation actor to the regulated pharmaceutical setting; receives escalated clinical or product-quality questions.

elements.text: Sales Administrator
elements.justification: Reuses the distribution pattern actor; handles commercial escalations and order entry when the assistant must not answer.

elements.text: Hospital Buyer
elements.justification: Adapts the 'Customer' actor; is the only party who can confirm an order, as required by the query constraint.

elements.text: The ordering assistant runs on an external model provider outside the organization's infrastructure
elements.justification: Stated in the query; no retrieved pattern carries it explicitly, and it motivates the data-minimisation task and constraint.

elements.text: Hospital buyers act on the assistant's answers when placing orders for medicines
elements.justification: Adapts the pattern belief 'Customers act on the assistant's answers'; it justifies the high correctness target and the escalation rule.

elements.text: Prices and contract terms are hospital specific
elements.justification: Adapts the belief 'Price lists are customer specific'; it is the reason cross-hospital price disclosure must be zero.

elements.text: The assistant cannot place or change an order without the hospital buyer's explicit confirmation
elements.justification: Query constraint, aligned with the pattern constraint that the assistant does not commit the company financially.

elements.text: Patient identifiers are never sent to the language model provider
elements.justification: Query constraint, adapted from the pattern constraint limiting customer personal data sent to the model provider.

elements.text: Only approved and currently valid documents may enter the retrieval corpus; drafts and expired contracts are excluded
elements.justification: Carries over the pattern's conflict resolution (broader corpus versus unapproved drafts), keeping the citation KPI meaningful while escalation covers the gaps.

elements.text: A model or prompt change cannot be released without approval by a second approver recorded in the change register
elements.justification: Adapts 'Payment runs need a second approver' to the AI release gate, making the 100% pre-release approval target enforceable.

elements.text: An answer without a citation from the approved corpus cannot be shown to the hospital buyer
elements.justification: Adapts the attributability principle of the governance pattern into a hard output rule supporting the 100% citation target.

output.rational_statement: G07 makes the LLM-based ordering assistant a governed component of the regulated order-to-delivery chain of G01: because the assistant runs on an external model provider and hospital buyers act on its answers, each of its failure modes is turned into a controlled and measurable mechanism. Restricting retrieval to the approved product, contract and regulatory corpus, citing the source on every answer, blocking uncited answers and escalating out-of-scope or clinical questions to the Responsible Pharmacist or Sales Administrator make the answers traceable and give evidence for G07-K1; the fixed monthly evaluation test set reviewed by the Quality Assurance Officer supplies the correctness evidence for G07-K3. Entitlement-filtered retrieval against hospital-specific contract price lists, combined with the monthly audit of interaction logs by the IT Security Officer and the removal of patient identifiers before any call to the provider, keep the regulated and commercially confidential data inside its boundary, which is what G07-K2 verifies. The change register, the pre-release approval with a second approver and the periodic AI risk review with the Data Protection Officer make every model or prompt change attributable and reversible, which G07-K4 measures. Finally, the constraint that no order is created or changed without the hospital buyer's confirmation keeps the human accountable for every transaction, so the assistant accelerates ordering without weakening the control and security that the parent goal G01 requires.
